name: Security Incidents
blurb: Major AI security events as they are disclosed.

reading.body:
Lambda has reported incidents in 62 of 93 observed periods, a rate nearly ten times higher than any other provider in this dataset, and carried a peak of three simultaneous open incidents where every other tracked provider peaked at one.

The six providers shown here are not a complete picture: the data covers 12 providers in total but supplies per-provider breakdowns for only six. Among those six, incident frequency varies sharply. ElevenLabs and Baseten each recorded incidents in 3 of 99 observed periods. OpenAI recorded incidents in 9, Fireworks AI in 10, Anthropic in 4. Lambda's 62 of 93 puts it in a different category entirely, though the data does not explain whether that reflects a higher underlying incident rate, more thorough disclosure, or a different classification of what counts as an incident.

The daily series runs from August 14 to August 31, 2026, and shows a clear drop in aggregate daily incidents across that window, from a range of two to four in the earlier days to zero or one by the final days. One incident remained open at the time of generation. The data records counts of disclosed events, not their severity, duration, or cause, so it cannot speak to whether these incidents affected model inference, data integrity, or infrastructure availability. For a site tracking how compute and power constrain AI scaling, security incidents represent a separate failure mode that the daily series captures in frequency only.
